page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32 is a high-memory instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Operating on x86_64 architecture, the processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The configuration is equipped with 248 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external persistent disks for data retention, and features zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced general-purpose compute metrics alongside strong vectorized performance. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 47956.79 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15636.0, both placing within middle-tier averages. Leveraging AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, the system performs exceptionally well in lightweight inference workloads, registering 421.19 tokens per second for small 135M model text generation and 2850.19 tokens per second for prompt processing. Static web throughput reached 51.15 GB/sec, while database throughput reached 16512.4 operations in PassMark testing and 39.05 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks.

The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated accelerators establishes clear operational tradeoffs. Running large generative models exposes compute limitations, with 70B parameter text generation falling to 2.38 tokens per second. However, the high memory-to-core allocation provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for architectures where RAM capacity is the principal constraint. The c4-highmem-32 is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, Redis cache deployments, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-concurrency web servers.
